title: Capstone: Multi-File Math Library
description:
**Goal:** Build your own little library split across files. The seven files are already in the explorer on the left of the editor, each with a short note saying what belongs in it.

| File | What goes in it |
|---|---|
| `main.cpp` | A menu that uses all three modules |
| `geometry.h` and `geometry.cpp` | Area, perimeter and volume functions |
| `convert.h` and `convert.cpp` | Unit conversions |
| `io.h` and `io.cpp` | `getInt()`, `getDouble()`, `printResult()` |

A header (`.h`) holds **declarations**: the promise that a function exists. Its `.cpp` holds the **definitions**: the code itself. Press **Run** and Xenon compiles every `.cpp` file in the explorer and links them into one program, which is exactly what listing them all on a compiler command line does.

starter.convert.cpp:
#include "convert.h"

// TODO: define the conversions declared in convert.h

hints: Do one module at a time. Declare `rectanglePerimeter` in `geometry.h`, define it in `geometry.cpp`, call it from `main`, press Run. When that works, the other functions are the same three steps.
`getDouble` is `getInt` with `double` instead of `int`. `printResult` could take a label and a value: `void printResult(std::string label, double value);`.

For the linker error: the compiler is happy because the header promised the function exists; the **linker** then finds no definition and reports an "unresolved external" (MSVC) or "undefined reference" (GCC). That is the difference between the two steps of a build (lesson 1.08).
requirements: Every `.cpp` includes its own header first
The program builds with no warnings (the Problems tab stays empty)
Deliberately cause a **linker error**: declare a function in a header, call it from `main.cpp`, but leave its definition out of the `.cpp`. Run, read the error, then fix it
stretch: put constants (like pi) in a header as `inline constexpr double pi{ 3.14159 };` (look up `constexpr`, covered in lesson 2.06, and why a header constant needs `inline`)
